_what_this_is: The entry gate, answered BEFORE drafting. The threshold question is whether a well-informed non-expert would confidently believe something the primary sources do not support.

belief._note: What the reader already believes, stated as they would state it. If you cannot write this sentence, there is nothing to correct and no subject -- which is how the tobacco-analogy candidate died.
belief.statement: For a depressed teenager, CBT works whichever way it is given: a course of sessions with a therapist, a group, a video call or an app or online programme all help about as much, so a cheaper or quicker format such as a self-help app or a group is a fair substitute for one-to-one therapy.
belief.how_we_know_they_believe_it: To be filled from coverage found during research (named outlets, quoted headlines), checked from page bytes.

what_the_sources_show._note: What the primary sources actually support, and which sources.

direction._note: CORRECTS, CONFIRMS or NARROWS. This field exists so the contrarianism guard can count. A publication whose answer is always CORRECTS is performing scepticism rather than assessing evidence, and is not to be trusted.
direction._expected_before_research: narrows (prediction, written before any source was opened; the recorded value is set after research)

reader_with_a_decision: A parent of a depressed teenager, or a GP, school counsellor or commissioner of child mental-health services, choosing between a waiting list for one-to-one CBT and a quicker or cheaper format (a group, therapy by video, or a self-help app or online course with or without a therapist checking in), who needs to know whether the format changes how much it helps.

public_record_check._note: NOT 'has anybody published this'. On any contested question, somebody has. The question is whether it has been carried WHERE THIS READER WOULD FIND IT. Run the counterexample hunter on the belief statement, not on the finding.
public_record_check.our_contribution: translation, extension, or correction of the prior art -- say which

kill_condition: There is no 'narrows' story, and the answer is CONFIRMS, if randomised trials or pooled analyses comparing CBT formats for depressed adolescents show that group, individual, remote and self-help (guided and unguided) formats work about equally well, with no format clearly better or worse. It is CORRECTS if the evidence shows that the format clearly matters in a way the belief denies (for example, unguided self-help clearly no better than control, or one-to-one clearly better than every other format). And it dies as a story if general coverage already carries the format comparison accurately where this reader would find it.

kill_condition_tested._note: Filled in AFTER going to look, by whoever looked.

lead_came_from: WHU reliability study draw (WHU-S02, issue.json); the question was given; the drawn source is not known to the drafting session.
